stem.text: The space probe Rosetta was designed to investigate a comet. The probe consisted of an orbiter and a lander. The orbiter had a mass of $170\,\text{kg}$ and the lander had a mass of $100\,\text{kg}$. When the two parts separated, the lander was pushed towards the surface of the comet so that its change in velocity towards the comet was $3.0\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.

stem.alt: Drawing of a central box with a segmented bar extending to each side, a smaller object below it with legs, and a downward arrow labelled 3.0 m s-1. Labels read orbiter mass 170 kg and lander mass 100 kg.

stem.text: Assume that the orbiter and lander were an isolated system.
The orbiter moved away from the comet during the separation.
What was the change in the speed of the orbiter?
